passages.provision_quote: A person … who is at least eighteen (18) years of age and is not otherwise prohibited from carrying or possessing a handgun … under state or federal law is not required to obtain or possess a license or permit from the state to carry a handgun in Indiana.
passages.note: The enrolled act removes Indiana's license-to-carry requirement, letting an adult not otherwise prohibited carry a handgun without a state license or permit.
The House bill-details page lists Robert Behning among the co-authors of HB 1296, the permitless-carry bill.
The House roll call on adopting HB 1296's conference committee report shows Behning voting Yea, 69-30, well above the near-unanimous threshold.

rows.reasoning: Behning co-authored HB 1296 (2022) and voted Yea to adopt its conference committee report; the enacted text removes Indiana's handgun carry license requirement, so a person not otherwise prohibited "is not required to obtain or possess a license or permit from the state to carry a handgun in Indiana." This matches the rung text "repeal major gun restrictions and let adults carry a firearm without a permit," and under the annex's rule for a state officeholder, removing the state's carry license meets both clauses.
